title: Agent Runner Orchestration
description: Extract and centralize the agent execution and orchestration logic into the tools library under `src/agentRunner/`. This provides clients with an easy-to-use `AgentRunnerTools` API to launch completions, manage complex tool lifecycles (send/resume/retry/abort), handle message preprocessing, and orchestrate isolated agents seamlessly — eliminating the need for each client to reimplement this logic themselves.

features.title: AgentRunnerTools Foundation & Abort Management
features.description:
Create the new module folder `src/agentRunner/` and introduce `src/agentRunner/AgentRunnerTools.ts` following the project's standard tool/module patterns. Establish the primary `AgentRunnerTools` surface and internal state for per-chat abort handling:

- Keep an internal `abortControllers: Record<string, AbortController>` keyed by `getChatContextKey(chatContext)`.
- Expose methods to create/cleanup abort signals and `abortCompletion(chatContext)`.
- Ensure abort cleanup is always run after completion flows terminate (success/error/abort).

Acceptance criteria:
- New folder/module structure exists and compiles.
- `AgentRunnerTools` can create an abort signal per chat context and abort an in-flight completion deterministically.
- No client needs to implement `AbortController` bookkeeping for completions.

features.title: Completion Pipeline & Preprocessing
features.description:
Implement the shared completion pipeline pieces inside `AgentRunnerTools`:

- `sendCompletion(chatContext, llmConfig, messages, systemPrompt)` convenience wrapper around `createCompletionTools().sendCompletion`.
- Message preprocessing:
  - Transform user messages with `files: string[]` into inline `@path` mentions appended to the content (tool messages pass through unchanged).
- LLM config enrichment:
  - If `LLMConfig` is missing pricing fields, enrich with costs using optional `LLMCostsTools.getPrice(provider, model)`.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clients can call `AgentRunnerTools.sendCompletion(...)` without reimplementing preprocessing/pricing logic.
- Preprocessing behavior matches the client manager: attachment lists become stable `Attached files:\n@...` blocks.
- LLM pricing enrichment is best-effort and non-fatal when costs data is absent.

features.title: Tool Orchestration Lifecycle (Send, Resume, Retry)
features.description:
Add tool-enabled completion orchestration to `AgentRunnerTools`, aligning with the client manager behavior:

- Implement `sendCompletionTools(...)` to:
  - Persist the user message via `ChatsTools.addChatMessages`.
  - Run a tool-calling completion loop via `createCompletionWithToolsParams(...)` + `completion.sendCompletionWithTools(...)`.
- Implement `retryCompletionTools(...)` by deleting the last chat message (via `ChatsTools.deleteLastMessage`) then re-running tool completion.
- Implement `resumeCompletionTools(...)` using `completion.resumeCompletionTools(...)` with provided `toolsGranted`.
- Include the "ignored trailing confirmations" behavior:
  - If a user sends a new message while there are trailing `tool` messages with `toolResult.type === 'require_confirmation'`, mark them as `not_allowed` and persist the updated chat history before continuing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Clients can send/resume/retry tool completions using only `AgentRunnerTools` + injected tool executor.
- Unconfirmed trailing tool calls are deterministically persisted as `not_allowed` when superseded by a new user message.
- Abort cleanup runs after each lifecycle method completes.

features.title: Tool Execution Routing Mechanism
features.description:
Define and implement the tool execution routing integration point for `AgentRunnerTools` so clients can plug in how tools are executed (e.g., via an orchestrator / tools manager / IPC bridge).

- Introduce a `callTool(toolCall: ToolCall, ctx: { projectId?: string; chatContext: ChatContext }) => Promise<any>` callback (exact signature TBD) that `AgentRunnerTools` uses during tool-enabled completion.
- Implement argument enrichment to match the client behavior:
  - If `chatContext.storyId` is set and the tool args do not contain `storyId`, inject it.
  - If `chatContext.featureId` is set and the tool args do not contain `featureId`, inject it.
  - (Optionally) design for projectId injection as a future extension (group chats etc).

Acceptance criteria:
- Tool execution can be fully delegated to the client via a single callback.
- `storyId`/`featureId` argument enrichment is applied consistently for all tool calls.
- The interface is documented and stable enough for external clients to implement easily.
